listenings.text: Right, quick update from the pricing side, two minutes. We narrowed the list down from forty categories to six, and we ruled out the three where the data is too thin. The pilot is running in the south, and we are scaling it up to two more regions next month. Two open points. First, we are phasing out the old spreadsheet, so if anyone is still using it, please stop this week. Second, I brought up the sign-off delay with the commercial director on Friday and she asked me to follow up on it with finance. I will report back on Thursday. That is everything from me.

Can I give you one piece of feedback before you go? In the meeting today, you had the strongest argument in the room and you did not push back once. When the finance director said the timeline was fine, you knew it was not, and you let it go. I understand why. In a second language, disagreeing costs more energy than agreeing. But here is the thing: if you do not bring it up in the room, it comes back three weeks later as a problem with your name on it. Next time, say one sentence. Just one. I would push back on the timeline, and here is why. That is enough.

paras: Team, a short update before Friday. We have narrowed the list down from forty categories to six, and we have ruled out the three where the data was too thin to trust. Nobody should read that as a failure: ruling something out early is a result.

The pilot in the south is holding. We are scaling it up to two more regions in March, with the same rollback plan we agreed in January. If adoption drops below sixty percent in any region, we pull it back and we look into why before we go any further.

Two things I need from you. We are phasing out the old spreadsheet at the end of the month, so please stop using it now, not in April. And if you disagree with any of the six categories we kept, bring it up this week, in the meeting, not afterwards in the corridor.
Last point. I brought the sign-off delay up with the commercial director on Friday, and she asked me to follow up on it with finance. I will report back on Thursday with a date.

gist.prompt: Read once for the main idea. What is the tone of this update?

A project on track, with two clear requests to the team
A manager announcing that the pilot has been cancelled
